plan.title: Coordinated Emergency Response Plan - Ward 18 Extreme Rainfall & Inundation
plan.operatorNote: Approved for immediate multi-department dispatch by Zone Counselor.

actions.recommendation: Reroute ambulance 108-B4 and queued units via Canal North corridor (0 citizen reports, currently clear) following the successful 2023 historical precedent, and override signals J14/J17 toward Canal North instead of Route R7.
actions.reason: Emergency unit 108-B4 carrying a STEMI patient is stationary 740 m from Ward 18 ER with only 14 minutes remaining in its intervention window, facing a 31-minute ETA via Hospital Road (4 km/hr speed). Traffic agent proposes diverting traffic via Route R7, but Citizen reports confirm knee-to-waist inundation with 6 vehicles already stalled at the R7 on-ramp, corroborated by Water telemetry showing R7 outfall depth at 138 cm (exceeding the 120 cm max). Three emergency units remain blocked without a clear path unless directed away from both Hospital Road and Route R7.
actions.expectedImpact: Mitigate Critical STEMI Mortality Risk from Blocked Ambulance Rerouted to Flooded R7 On-Ramp

actions.recommendation: Explicitly override and reject Traffic agent's Route R7 diversion plan; issue public transit advisory warning of R7 on-ramp stalling, and redirect flow toward Canal North.
actions.reason: A direct conflict exists between findings: Traffic agent recommends Route R7 as a viable diversion (18 km/hr speed, 620 vehicles/hr volume against 1800 capacity), whereas Citizen agent reports 41 inundation spots and 6 vehicles stalled at the R7 on-ramp, and Water agent confirms R7 outfall depth is 138 cm (exceeding 120 cm design max) with 'route_R7_saturated' flag. Diverting Hospital Road traffic (93% congestion) into saturated Route R7 under sustained 118 mm/hr rainfall (40-minute duration) risks trapping hundreds of vehicles in floodwater, repeating the October 2023 event that closed R7 for 6 hours.
actions.expectedImpact: Mitigate Conflicting Traffic Rerouting Protocol Leading to Mass Vehicle Entrapment on Route R7

actions.recommendation: Dispatch emergency field crew immediately for manual actuation of Gate 4N at Canal North before the 22-minute primary sump overflow threshold.
actions.reason: Stationary convective cell delivering 118 mm/hr rain (exceeding 45 mm/hr drain capacity) drives Ward 18 primary sump inflow to 390 m3/hr against 210 m3/hr pump capacity, bringing utilization to 96% with overflow projected in 22 minutes. Water agent indicates secondary relief via Canal North is required, but gate 4N requires manual actuation. Memory agent confirms Canal North diversion reduced historical sump levels by 34% within 15 minutes, and Citizen agent verifies Canal North currently has 0 reports and is clear; delay in manual dispatch will cause secondary overflow across Ward 18.
actions.expectedImpact: Mitigate Ward 18 Sump Overflow and Severe Inundation Caused by Manual Gate Actuation Delay

conflictsResolved.cost: rejected R7, adopted R9 (+1 min transit cost)

plan.gateReason: Confidence 70/100 — within range but not high enough, or not low-cost enough, for auto-execution.
unresolved: Ground verification of water supply contamination risk in Ward 18 due to lack of specific sensor evidence in current telemetry stream.
